Abstract

CSR has gained substantial consideration in management circles and has been linked to HRM in various ways. The study on how CSR would affect HRM, or the vice versa, has been of interest by many scholars. Much has been focusing on the conceptual framework and its application to the manufacturing sector, however, few studies have actually tried to establish empirical links between these areas. To fill this gap, we conducted a survey-based study where we looked at what the impact, if any, would be for a sample of 283 manufacturing firms located in the southern part of Malaysia. The result of the study revealed that there was no strong link between how CSR activities were practiced among these manufacturing firms and HRM practices. We also found that the HRM practices that were significantly related to CSR, such as training and performance appraisal, which might indicate that there is a lack of linkages between these areas. We recommend future research to investigate how CSR activities are linked to HRM practices among other industries. The findings from this research would be useful to organizations which are considering the integration between their CSR activities and HRM. The results would also be beneficial for HR practitioners, especially the ones in the manufacturing industry, on how they should apply or incorporate CSR activities into the practices they do for the organization.

Abstract

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization. Liquid chromatography at atmospheric pressure chemical ionization-mass spectrometry was utilized to identify three new diglucoside diesters and five already known monoglucoside monesters. These compounds were identified based on their accurate mass, and fragmentation patterns. In order to validate the structure of the unknowns, they were synthesized and further characterized. The results presented in this research are important for understanding the carotenoid chemistry of the snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis*.

We concluded that both multiple and single drug resistance exists in patients who have never been treated for leprosy. More studies should be conducted using larger patient pools with different degrees of leprosy infection.

**Abstract**

Objective: To investigate the variation of strength of the human mandible with the orientation to its long axis.
Methods: The human mandible is a living and anisotropic composite material. Three-dimensional tensile and compressive strength of it were determined using micro-tensile testing. Eighty human mandibles from individuals that died of natural causes, were collected. The test specimens were sectioned along 6 different planes, at 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, and 150° in reference to the longitudinal axis of the mandible. Uniaxial tension and compression tests were conducted, and the maximum loads required to break each specimen were recorded. Failure load data were statistically analyzed to determine which plane yielded the most and the least stress for both tensile and compressive loads. The stress distributions within each plane were evaluated and compared.
Results: In both tensile and compressive tests, the 150° plane had the highest average failure load; the 30° and the 90° planes had the lowest average failure load. The results suggest that the long axis and its perpendicular (90°) have a lower failure load, while the failure load is higher in planes 30°, 60°, and 150°. The results will be discussed in the context of the anatomical location of the mandibular condyle and its movements, as well as the force directions applied to the joint. 
Conclusion: The strength of the mandibule, when loaded to its failure, is higher on the sides than in its axis and perpendicular. Understanding these results could help improve the design of dental implant anchors.
